## Executive Summary

This survey provides a complete, line-by-line comparative analysis between `AF/Bulletin` and `AF/Business` to guide the implementation of R1 and R2.

1. **R1 (Content & Category Alignment)**: `AF/Bulletin` currently uses the outdated naming `mod_category` alongside `mod_content`. In `AF/Business`, category management is standardized under `mod_content_category`, with synchronized model relationships, SQL schemas, installer scripts, `ModuleRegistry`, `InstallerModuleCatalog`, frontend helpers, and admin templates. Additionally, `mod_content` in `AF/Business` includes hero slider integration (`slider` column and AJAX toggle) and FAQ binding (`$has_faq = true`).
2. **R2 (Core Modules Porting & Synchronization)**:
   - `mod_seo`: In `AF/Bulletin`, `mod_seo` is a legacy skeleton (339 lines) missing Google Search Console integration, robots.txt, sitemap generators, dynamic meta tag editors, dedicated assets (`mod_seo.js`, `mod_seo.css`), and the `google_settings.twig` template present in `AF/Business` (643 lines).
   - `mod_faq` & `mod_faq_mod`: Entirely **missing** in `AF/Bulletin`. Needs full porting of backend controllers, models, validators, language files across 8+ languages, SQL schemas, installer manifests, admin mobile-first modal interface (`templates/admin/mod_faq/modal_list.twig`), dedicated assets (`mod_faq.js`, `mod_faq.css`), and frontend Twig macro (`templates/default/macros/faq.twig`).
   - `mod_newsletter`: Entirely **missing** in `AF/Bulletin`. Needs full porting of controller with self-healing schema creation, ORM model, SQL schema, 9-language translation files, installer manifest, admin list template, and modal sheet integration (`modal_newsletter.js`).
   - `mod_settings`: `AF/Bulletin` contains a legacy version (1018 lines) with Turkish identifiers/methods (`$this->tema`, `Registry::getir()`, `$this->tema->veri()`), lacking self-healing column bootstrap, legal information management (`legal_info.twig`, `legal_info.js`, `legal_info.css`), animated logo handlers, site status management, and statistics configuration found in `AF/Business` (2061 lines).
   - **Admin Modal Engine Architecture**: `AF/Business` has modularized all AJAX dialogs into `templates/admin/assets/js/modals/` (`af_modal_engine.js`, `modal_user_menu.js`, `modal_user_profile.js`, `modal_newsletter.js`, `modal_redirects.js`, `modal_site_status.js`, `modal_theme_logo.js`) and `templates/admin/assets/css/modals/core_modals.css`, eliminating inline CSS/JS bloat.

### 2.2 Detailed Module Specifications for R2

#### 1. `mod_seo`
- **Controller**: `mod/mod_seo/index.php` (643 lines)
  - Features: Google Search Console OAuth & API metrics fetching, XML sitemap generator, `robots.txt` generator, dynamic header meta tag injector, automatic data directory schema initialization (`seo_settings.json`).
- **Templates**: `list.twig`, `settings.twig`, `google_settings.twig`.
- **Assets**: `templates/admin/assets/js/mod_seo.js`, `templates/admin/assets/css/mod_seo.css`.
- **Permissions**: `list`, `settings`, `google_settings`.

#### 2. `mod_faq` & `mod_faq_mod`
- **Architecture**: Polymorphic FAQ attachment engine. Any module (e.g. `mod_content`, `mod_news`, `mod_publication`) can attach interactive FAQs to individual records via AJAX modal (`/mod_faq/modal_list?mod_name=...&vid=...`).
- **Controllers**:
  - `mod_faq_mod`: Manages entity-level FAQ items (`question`, `answer`, `status`, `sort_order`, `mod_name`, `vid`).
  - `mod_faq_mod_mod`: Registry controller defining which framework modules support FAQ integration.
- **Frontend Twig Macro**: `templates/default/macros/faq.twig` with `render(faqs, title)` for responsive accordion UI and `schema(faqs)` for Google Rich Snippets (`FAQPage` JSON-LD).
- **Admin UI**: Phone-first touch drag-and-drop reordering with Sortable.js, live char counters, status switch, batch saving.

#### 3. `mod_newsletter`
- **Controller**: `mod/mod_newsletter/index.php` extending `BaseModuleController` with self-healing SQLite/MySQL table creation.
- **Admin UI**: Dedicated subscriber list with live search, status badge filter (`active`, `unsubscribed`), CSV export, batch/single deletion.
- **Modal Engine Integration**: `modal_newsletter.js` allows administrators to view and manage newsletter subscriber counts directly from the top app bar header menu without full page reloads.

#### 4. `mod_settings`
- **Controller**: `mod/mod_settings/index.php` (2061 lines)
  - Full modern administration controller supporting:
    - Site title, description, keywords, contact info per language.
    - Site status toggle (Open vs Under Maintenance) with custom maintenance HTML/reason.
    - Company legal information (`legal_info.twig` / `legal_info.js` / `legal_info.css`).
    - Dynamic logo, favicon, dark-mode logo, and animated SVG/JSON logo management.
    - Social media link bindings (`mod_settings_social`).
    - Company statistics counters (`stat_completed_projects`, `stat_ongoing_projects`, `stat_workforce`, `stat_offices`).
  - Strict English codebase standard: eliminates legacy `$this->tema`, `Registry::getir()`, and `$this->tema->veri()`.

## 3. Dependencies, Shared Libraries, and Interface Contracts

### 3.1 Framework Core Libraries (`lib/`)
- `BaseModuleController`: Required base class for `mod_content`, `mod_faq`, `mod_faq_mod`, `mod_newsletter`. Handles standard CRUD, datatable JSON responses, image upload pipelines, and relation syncs.
- `ORM`: Active Record abstraction used across all models (`mod_content_model`, `contents_model`, `mod_content_category_model`, `mod_faq_model`, `mod_newsletter_model`, `mod_settings_model`).
- `Database`: Core database abstraction supporting MySQL / SQLite / PostgreSQL adapters with `fetch_array()`, `query()`, `get_connection()`.
- `AdminTemplate`: Modern template engine binding Twig context, handling language loading, and setting page variables (`$this->theme->set()`, `$this->theme->lang()`).
- `ModuleRegistry`: Dependency mapping class. Must register `mod_content_category`, `newsletter.subscribe`, and remove all references to deprecated modules.
- `Registry`: Global runtime registry. Must strictly use standard methods: `Registry::get()`, `Registry::add()`, `Registry::has()`, `Registry::set()`, `Registry::remove()`.

### 3.2 Database Schemas & Table Dependencies
1. `mod_content_category`:
   - Columns: `id`, `lang`, `name`, `parent_id`, `order`, `root`, `seo`, `title`, `keywords`, `description`, `menu`, `image`, `user_id`, `acl_id`.
2. `mod_content`:
   - Columns: `id`, `lang`, `name`, `category_id`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deck`, `summary`, `content`, `seo`, `title`, `keywords`, `description`, `gallery_id`, `file_id`, `image`, `acl_id`, `video`, `user_id`, `slider`.
3. `contents` (SQL View):
   - Joins `mod_content`, `mod_user`, `mod_user_group`, and `mod_content_category`.
4. `mod_faq` & `mod_faq_mod`:
   - `mod_faq`: `id`, `mod_name`, `vid`, `lang`, `question`, `answer`, `status`, `sort_order`, `user_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.
   - `mod_faq_mod`: `id`, `name`, `mod_name`, `mod_key`, `mod_value`.
5. `mod_newsletter`:
   - `id`, `email`, `lang`, `source`, `status`, `ip_address`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.
6. `mod_settings` & `mod_settings_social`:
   - Complete site configuration schema with legal info and statistics columns.

### 3.3 Routing, Permissions & Security Contracts

| Module | Route Prefix | Required Roles / Permissions |
|---|---|---|
| `mod_content` | `/mod_content/...` | `list`, `add`, `edit`, `delete`, `gallery`, `file`, `edit_status`, `change_status`, `approval`, `moderate_edit`, `moderate_delete`, `video_download` |
| `mod_content_category` | `/mod_content_category/...` | `list`, `add`, `edit`, `delete`, `moderate_edit`, `moderate_delete` |
| `mod_seo` | `/seo`, `/seo/settings`, `/seo/google_settings` | `list`, `settings`, `google_settings` |
| `mod_faq` | `/mod_faq/...` | `list`, `add`, `edit`, `delete`, `reorder` |
| `mod_faq_mod` | `/mod_faq_mod/...` | `list`, `add`, `edit`, `delete` |
| `mod_newsletter` | `/mod_newsletter/...` | `list`, `delete` |
| `mod_settings` | `/mod_settings/edit`, `/mod_settings/legal_info`, `/mod_settings/social_media` | `edit`, `settings_edit`, `legal_info` |

## 4. Architectural & Quality Policy Compliance Check

1. **Strict Code Separation Mandate**:
   - In `AF/Bulletin`, several templates (`list.twig`, `sheets_extra.twig`) contain inline `<style>` tags. During the synchronization from `AF/Business`, all styles must be kept inside separate CSS files (`templates/admin/assets/css/` and `modals/core_modals.css`).
2. **Phone-First Admin Surface**:
   - All ported admin interfaces (`mod_faq/modal_list.twig`, `mod_newsletter/list.twig`, `mod_settings/legal_info.twig`, `mod_seo/google_settings.twig`) are built strictly for mobile touch navigation with 44px+ tap targets, floating bottom bars, and swipeable sheets.
3. **Language & Identifier Standardization**:
   - All Turkish comments, legacy method names (`getir`, `tema`, `veri`, `rolls`, `insert_roll`), and Turkish array keys (`durum`, `anasayfa`) must be purged and replaced with English standards.
4. **Multilingual Support**:
   - All ported modules must provide comprehensive translation definitions across Kurdish (`ku`), English (`en`), Turkish (`tr`), Zaza (`zza`), Sorani (`ckb`), German (`de`), Arabic (`ar`), and French (`fr`).
